purpose: How a business internet and wireless agent reasons about which carrier partner programs to enter and carry - who bills, who supports, and who owns the account under each channel model - and how to turn one small-business customer into several honest revenue streams through verified program terms, discovery-grounded bundle design, and disclosure-first account planning that stops where site qualification and lifecycle management begin.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

carrier partner-program terms, compensation plans and product availability change without notice; every quoted commitment presumes a same-cycle check of the current program guide, never a remembered version

compensation is described only as mechanism classes (activation/upfront, residual/ongoing, account-based, chargeback/clawback) or qualitative bands; no specific commission figure, price, or account multiple is ever stated as fact

the default channel model is agency: the carrier bills the customer, provides tier-one support, and owns the retail account, while the agent is compensated under the program agreement; deviations (reseller, referral) are treated explicitly

content is educational and operational for the agent-operator, not personalized financial, legal, or tax advice; program-specific and jurisdiction-specific obligations must be verified against the current agreement and local rules before acting
exclusions: address-level serviceability and coverage checks, site surveys, ordering, provisioning and activation coordination, failover configuration and testing, and install handoff - that is the site qualification and service activation KB this one hands candidate designs to

compensation tracking and reconciliation, renewals, upgrades and technology refresh cycles, churn and win-back, customer-carrier escalation handling, and protecting the compensation stream through program compliance - that is the account compensation and lifecycle KB downstream
stating specific commission rates, prices, promo amounts, or account revenue multiples as fact; compensation and pricing appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands with a verification path
any representation that the agent is the carrier, or selling products the current program agreement does not authorize the agent to sell
residential and consumer sales, and personalized financial, legal, tax, or insurance advice to the customer or the operator

competency_questions.question: Under agent, reseller, and referral channel models, who bills the customer, who takes the support call, and who owns the account - and which model fits an operator of my size?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_MODEL_MAP states billing, support, and account ownership per model and the consequences each split has for compensation, liability, and customer relationship

competency_questions.question: How do I verify what a carrier program currently offers and pays before I commit anything to a customer, given that program guides change without notice?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROGRAM_TERM_VERIFICATION names the artifacts to check (current program guide, comp plan bulletin, product availability notice), the recheck cadence, and the rule that no commitment is issued against a remembered version

competency_questions.question: How does an operator qualify into a carrier program, and when is entering through a master agent or distributor the better route than a direct agreement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROGRAM_ENTRY_QUALIFICATION lists the entry requirement classes and MASTER_AGENT_ROUTE weighs the split mechanism and back-office support against the weaker direct carrier relationship, decided by realistic volume

competency_questions.question: Which carrier programs should I carry, and when does adding a second carrier help rather than dilute my standing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_PORTFOLIO_SELECTION gives the selection criteria (footprint fit, product breadth, comp mechanism fit, program stability, channel-conflict exposure) and MULTI_CARRIER_BALANCE gives the documented-gap rule for adding a program

competency_questions.question: How do activation, residual, and account-based compensation mechanisms differ, and how does the mechanism mix decide which deals are worth pursuing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMP_MECHANISM_LITERACY explains each mechanism class and its chargeback exposure without invented figures, and DEAL_ECONOMICS_SCREEN turns the mix into a go/no-go screen per deal

competency_questions.question: What do account ownership and rules of engagement mean for whom I may pursue, and how do I keep a worked deal from being taken by carrier direct or another agent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_CONFLICT_AND_ACCOUNT_OWNERSHIP explains ownership per model, the opportunity-registration mechanism, and what to do when a prospect is already claimed

competency_questions.question: Which small-business segments does the internet-plus-wireless-backup bundle actually fit, and why those?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEGMENT_TARGETING names segment profiles (transaction-dependent retail and food service, multi-site operators, field trades, professional offices) tied to the operational reason the bundle pays for itself in each

competency_questions.question: What must honest needs discovery establish before anything is proposed, and what selling behaviors are off limits regardless of the deal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISCOVERY_FACT_BASE lists the facts to capture (current services and contract end dates, downtime cost in the customer's own numbers, sites, lines, applications, decision makers) and ETHICAL_SELLING_GUARDRAILS states the disclosure-first, no-fear-selling, vulnerable-customer rules

competency_questions.question: How do I design a bundle and account plan that turns one customer into several revenue streams without overselling a small operator?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUNDLE_ARCHITECTURE lays out the layered anchor-plus-attach structure and ACCOUNT_REVENUE_PLAN sequences attaches against discovery facts and contract timing, with the right-sizing rule for the smallest customers

competency_questions.question: How do I position wireless backup honestly - from the customer's own downtime facts - rather than by selling fear of outages?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BACKUP_ATTACH_STRATEGY derives the case from the customer's stated cost of a down hour and their outage history, and blocks the attach when discovery shows tolerable downtime

competency_questions.question: What must a proposal disclose before signature, and how is the agent's relationship to the carrier represented truthfully?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROPOSAL_DISCLOSURE_PACK lists the mandatory disclosures (term, early-termination exposure class, promo roll-off mechanics, who bills, who supports, serviceability-pending status) and AFFILIATION_INTEGRITY states the authorized-agent representation rule

competency_questions.question: When and how do business mobile lines and adjacent services like managed Wi-Fi and cameras attach to the anchor account?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOBILITY_ATTACH explains the per-line ongoing mechanism and timing off the anchor relationship, and ADJACENT_SERVICES_ATTACH bounds attaches to products the current program authorizes

competency_questions.question: What exactly does bundle strategy hand to site qualification, and why is every proposal contingent until the address is verified?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICEABILITY_CONTINGENCY_HANDOFF defines the handoff package (addresses, candidate services, constraints) and the rule that serviceability is address-specific fact-finding never assumed from coverage maps

competency_questions.question: Where does this KB stop - what does the account plan hand to lifecycle management, and what does bundle strategy deliberately not do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_PLAN_LIFECYCLE_HANDOFF names the handoff contents (expected stream map by mechanism class, contract dates, attach roadmap) and states that tracking, renewals, and escalation belong downstream

glossary.definition: A carrier channel program in which the agent sells under the carrier's brand while the carrier bills the customer, provides tier-one support, and owns the retail account; the agent is compensated per the program agreement through activation and ongoing mechanisms.

An intermediary holding direct contracts with many carriers that sub-contracts smaller agents; it grants faster program access and back-office support in exchange for a share of the compensation, and its terms govern the sub-agent's rights.

A channel model in which the operator buys the service wholesale, bills the customer under its own brand, and takes the support call; it owns the customer relationship but also the credit, billing, and support burden the agency model leaves with the carrier.
The lightest channel model: the operator passes a lead to the carrier and is paid a one-time fee when it closes, with no billing, support, or account role and usually no ongoing compensation stream.

The upfront mechanism class: a payment triggered by a service being installed and activated, typically subject to a chargeback window if the customer cancels early; it front-loads cash but carries clawback exposure.

The ongoing mechanism classes: recurring payment computed from the account's billed revenue or its active lines/services for as long as the account stays in good standing and the agent remains compliant with the program.

The program mechanism that recovers previously paid compensation when a triggering condition occurs within a defined window - early cancellation, non-payment, or a disqualified sale; its length and triggers are program-specific and must be read from the current guide.

The program's published boundaries between the agent channel, carrier direct sales, and other partners: who may pursue which accounts, how disputes are decided, and what an existing registration means for a new pursuer.

The mechanism by which an agent records a named prospect with the carrier or master agent so the pursuit is protected for a period against carrier direct and other agents; unregistered work is unprotected work.

Adding a further service - wireless backup, mobile lines, managed Wi-Fi, cameras - onto an existing anchor account, creating an additional compensation stream and raising the account's switching cost.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for carrier_programs_and_bundle_strategy work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Map the three channel models an operator can occupy and what each splits between agent and carrier: in the agency model the carrier bills, handles tier-one support, and owns the retail account while the agent earns activation plus ongoing compensation; in the reseller model the operator buys wholesale, bills under its own brand, owns the customer, and absorbs support and credit risk; in the referral model the operator passes a lead for a one-time fee and holds no account role. Every downstream choice - what compensation can exist, who the customer calls, what the agent may promise - is determined by which model the signed agreement actually establishes, so the map is built first and each carried program is placed on it explicitly.

included: billing, support, and account-ownership split per model
compensation and liability consequences of each split
placing each carried program on the map
excluded: the mechanics of any one program's comp plan
wholesale cost negotiation for a reseller operation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carried program's agreement changes who bills, who supports, or who owns the account

pros.claim: Knowing who bills and who supports before selling prevents promising service the agent cannot deliver
pros.example: an agency-model agent tells a restaurant the carrier's support line handles outages instead of implying he runs a help desk

cons.claim: The clean three-model map blurs in practice because programs mix elements
cons.example: an agency program that still routes first-line billing questions to the agent for the first sixty days

failure_modes: selling as if the agent owns the account when the carrier does, then over-promising support
entering a reseller agreement without pricing in the billing and support burden it transfers
acceptance_tests: each carried program is classified agent, reseller, or referral with its billing, support, and ownership split written down and reflected in every customer-facing promise
revisit_triggers: a carrier restructures its channel and migrates agents to a different model
the operator considers adding a reseller or referral line alongside agency deals

nodes.definition: Institutionalize the rule that partner-program terms, compensation plans, and product availability change without notice, so no commitment to a customer or a carrier is made from memory. The discipline names the artifacts that count as current truth - the program guide in the partner portal, the latest comp plan bulletin, product availability and end-of-sale notices, and promo terms with their expiry - and requires a same-cycle check of each before quoting, proposing, or signing. A remembered rate, a screenshot from last quarter, or a master agent's verbal summary is treated as stale until re-verified, and the check itself is logged so a later dispute can show what the program said on the day of commitment.

included: which artifacts constitute current program truth
the pre-commitment recheck rule and its logging
treating remembered or second-hand terms as stale
excluded: tracking whether paid compensation matches the plan
negotiating custom terms with the carrier

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a program guide revision, comp plan bulletin, promo expiry, or product end-of-sale notice is published

pros.claim: A dated verification log turns a later comp or pricing dispute into a records check instead of an argument
pros.example: when a promo is honored differently than quoted, the agent produces the program bulletin as it read on proposal day

cons.claim: Re-verifying every quote adds friction that tempts shortcuts on small deals
cons.example: skipping the portal check for a single-line add and quoting a retired promo

failure_modes: quoting last quarter's comp plan or promo after the program changed it
committing a product that went end-of-sale, forcing a walk-back after signature
acceptance_tests: every issued quote or proposal carries the date and source of its program-terms check, and no commitment references a guide version older than the current one
revisit_triggers: the carrier or master agent publishes a program guide revision or comp plan bulletin
a quote is contradicted by the portal at order time

nodes.definition: Represent the relationship to the carrier exactly as the program defines it: the operator is an authorized agent selling the carrier's service under the program's rules, not the carrier itself and not an independent network operator. This governs business cards, storefront signage, web copy, proposals, and the words used in a pitch - the carrier's marks are used only as the brand guidelines permit, the agent's own business name stays distinct, and any customer confusion about who they are buying from is corrected on the spot. It also bounds what may be sold: only products the current agreement authorizes, with anything outside it referred rather than improvised, because misrepresentation is a program-termination offense that can forfeit the ongoing compensation the whole business stands on.

included: authorized-agent representation in all customer-facing material
carrier brand usage within program guidelines
selling only what the current agreement authorizes
excluded: the full proposal disclosure list
trademark law analysis beyond following the program's brand rules

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the program's representation or brand-usage rules change, or a compliance notice arrives

pros.claim: Clean affiliation framing protects the program relationship that all ongoing compensation depends on
pros.example: a storefront sign reading authorized agent of the carrier rather than the carrier's logo standing alone survives a program compliance review

cons.claim: Honest agent framing can feel weaker in the pitch than implying carrier status
cons.example: a prospect who wanted to deal with the carrier directly hesitates when the agent clarifies the relationship

failure_modes: web copy or signage that implies the operator is the carrier
improvising a sale of a product the agreement does not authorize to keep a customer
acceptance_tests: all customer-facing materials pass the program's brand and representation rules, and every product on a proposal appears in the current authorization list
revisit_triggers: the program's brand guidelines or authorized product list change
a customer's words reveal they believe they are dealing with the carrier directly

nodes.definition: Fix the selling rules that bind every other node: disclosure comes before persuasion, fear is never the sales lever, and the smallest or least sophisticated customers get extra care rather than extra pressure. Concretely - material terms (contract length, early-termination exposure class, promo roll-off, who bills and supports) are raised by the agent before the customer asks; outage risk is discussed only from the customer's own operational facts, never as manufactured dread; a single-owner shop, a buyer working in a second language, or an obviously rushed decision-maker triggers plain-language explanation, a smaller starting bundle, and explicit permission to take the proposal away and read it. The guardrails exist because an agency business lives on multi-year account relationships and program standing, both of which one pressured sale can destroy.

included: disclosure-before-persuasion ordering
prohibition on fear-based outage selling
care rules for vulnerable or unsophisticated buyers
excluded: the specific proposal disclosure checklist
consumer-protection legal analysis beyond the obligation class, which must be verified in the operator's jurisdiction

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: complaint or churn evidence tied to selling behavior, or a change in applicable consumer-protection obligations

pros.claim: Fit-first selling produces accounts that stay, which is what ongoing compensation mechanisms actually reward
pros.example: a right-sized two-service start at a bakery renews and later adds lines, while an oversold five-service bundle would have churned inside the chargeback window

cons.claim: Guardrails slow closes and concede short-term revenue that a pushier competitor may take
cons.example: a rival agent closes the rushed buyer the same day with an oversized bundle the guardrails would have trimmed

failure_modes: leading with outage horror stories instead of the customer's own downtime numbers
loading a micro-business with services discovery never supported because the comp mix favored them
acceptance_tests: every proposal shows material terms disclosed before close, the backup case cites the customer's own downtime facts, and small-buyer deals show the right-sizing rule was applied
revisit_triggers: a complaint, cancellation reason, or chargeback pattern suggests pressured or misunderstood sales
consumer-protection obligations in the operator's jurisdiction change

nodes.definition: Understand compensation as mechanism classes rather than numbers: activation/upfront pays once when a service installs and activates, and is exposed to a chargeback window if the customer cancels early; residual pays recurringly as a function of the account's billed revenue for as long as the account survives and the agent stays compliant; account-based/per-line pays recurringly per active line or service on the account. Each program mixes these differently, and the mix - not any single rate - determines the shape of the business: activation-heavy programs reward volume and suffer from churn, residual and account-based programs reward retention and bundle depth. What each class pays in a given program is a fact to read from the current guide per deal, never to assert from memory or hearsay, and never to state to anyone as a fixed figure.

included: the activation, residual, and account-based mechanism classes
chargeback/clawback exposure per class
how the mechanism mix shapes which selling behavior is rewarded
excluded: tracking or reconciling actual payments against the plan
any specific rate, percentage, or dollar figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carried program's compensation mechanism mix or chargeback conditions are restated

pros.claim: Mechanism literacy lets the operator predict how a program will treat a sale before making it
pros.example: recognizing that an activation-heavy program makes a shaky month-to-month customer a likely net loss once the chargeback window is considered

cons.claim: Mechanism classes abstract over program quirks that only the current guide reveals
cons.example: a program whose ongoing payments require the agent to remain the account's registered partner, a condition the class description alone would miss

failure_modes: reasoning from an invented or remembered rate instead of the current guide
building the business on activation cash while ignoring the chargeback exposure it carries
acceptance_tests: each carried program has its mechanism mix and chargeback conditions summarized from the current guide with the read date, and no artifact anywhere states a specific figure as fact
revisit_triggers: a program restates its compensation structure or chargeback windows
a new program with a different mechanism mix is considered

nodes.definition: Work out how the operator actually gets into a program and what entry costs. Entry requirement classes recur across carriers: a registered business entity in good standing, tax and banking documentation, signed program and confidentiality agreements, product and compliance training or certification, and sometimes a volume expectation or an existing book of business for direct entry. The qualification decision is which door to use - apply directly to the carrier's partner program, or enter as a sub-agent under a master agent or distributor whose contract already exists - and the answer follows from the operator's realistic near-term volume, back-office capacity, and appetite for the obligations a direct agreement imposes. Requirements are program-specific and change, so the current application terms are read at decision time rather than assumed from another carrier's pattern.

included: entry requirement classes across carrier programs
the direct-versus-distributor door decision inputs
reading current application terms at decision time
excluded: the master agent route's internal economics, treated in its own unit
carrier selection among programs already accessible

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a program's entry requirements, intake status, or agreement terms change

pros.claim: Treating entry as requirement classes lets the operator prepare one clean dossier that serves every application
pros.example: entity documents, tax forms, and proof of insurance assembled once and reused across two carrier applications and a distributor onboarding

cons.claim: Requirement classes understate how much direct-entry bars vary by carrier and cycle
cons.example: one carrier admitting new solo agents freely while another quietly requires an established book before granting direct status

failure_modes: applying direct with no realistic volume and being rejected or shelved, losing months
signing program agreements unread and discovering exclusivity or conduct clauses later
acceptance_tests: for each targeted program the entry route is chosen with its requirement list, obligations, and application status recorded from the current terms
revisit_triggers: a targeted program changes its entry requirements or pauses new-agent intake
the operator's volume or capacity changes enough to reopen the direct-versus-distributor choice

nodes.definition: Evaluate entering carrier programs through a master agent or technology services distributor instead of directly. The route trades a share of compensation - the split mechanism is defined in the sub-agent agreement, not invented - for immediate access to many carriers under one contract, quoting and order support, commission administration, and an escalation path the solo operator lacks. Its risks are structural: the sub-agent's rights exist only through the master's contract, so a master being acquired, changing its splits, or ending a carrier relationship reshapes the operator's business overnight; and the carrier knows the master, not necessarily the agent, which weakens the operator's standing if it later wants direct status. The evaluation reads the sub-agent agreement for split mechanics, payment timing class, account portability on exit, and what happens to ongoing compensation if either side terminates.

included: what the distributor route provides and what it takes
sub-agent agreement terms that matter: splits as mechanism, payment timing class, exit portability
structural dependency risks of selling through a master
excluded: which carriers to carry once access exists
any specific split percentage or payment figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the sub-agent agreement, the master's carrier lineup, or the operator's volume position changes

pros.claim: One distributor contract opens multiple carrier programs a new operator could not enter directly
pros.example: a first-year agent quoting three carriers' business internet through a single master relationship while direct applications would still be pending

cons.claim: The split permanently reduces every stream and the master's contract is a single point of failure
cons.example: a master agent acquisition that re-papers sub-agent terms mid-year and changes how ongoing compensation flows

failure_modes: signing a sub-agent agreement without reading exit and portability terms
staying on the distributor split long after volume would justify direct status
acceptance_tests: the sub-agent agreement's split mechanism, payment timing class, termination handling, and account portability are summarized in writing before signature
revisit_triggers: the master changes splits, is acquired, or drops a carrier
the operator's volume approaches the class of levels where direct entry becomes realistic

nodes.definition: Choose the small set of carrier programs the operator actively sells, scored against the business it intends to build: footprint fit (does the carrier's wired and fixed-wireless coverage plausibly serve the operator's target geography, to be proven per address later), product breadth (can one program cover primary internet, wireless backup, mobility, and the attach services the bundle needs), compensation mechanism fit (does the mix reward the retention-and-bundle model rather than pure activation volume), program stability (history of honoring ongoing compensation and of channel-friendly conduct), and channel-conflict exposure (how aggressively the carrier's direct teams work the same segment). The output is a deliberate portfolio - often one lead program plus a complement - with the reasons recorded, because an unchosen portfolio drifts toward whichever program shouted loudest.

included: the five selection criteria and their weighing
the lead-plus-complement portfolio decision with recorded reasons
channel-conflict exposure as a selection input
excluded: address-level serviceability proof, which belongs to site qualification
ongoing portfolio rebalancing, treated in the multi-carrier unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carried or candidate program's footprint, product set, mechanism mix, or conduct changes

pros.claim: A deliberately chosen lead program concentrates learning, volume, and program standing where they compound
pros.example: an operator whose installs sit with one carrier reaches that program's better support tier while a scattered book stays anonymous everywhere

cons.claim: Concentration exposes the whole book to one program's changes
cons.example: a lead carrier tightening its ongoing-compensation eligibility rules touches nearly every account at once

failure_modes: carrying whichever program recruited hardest instead of scoring against the intended business
choosing on headline compensation while ignoring footprint fit for the actual target geography
acceptance_tests: the portfolio decision record scores each candidate program on all five criteria and names the lead program and each complement's role
revisit_triggers: a carried program materially changes its terms, footprint, or product set
serviceability results or lost deals show the portfolio mismatches the target geography

nodes.definition: Know who owns an account under each program and how a pursued deal is protected. In the agency model the carrier owns the retail account, but programs still track which partner is credited with it, and their rules of engagement define the boundaries between the agent channel, carrier direct sales, national retail, and other partners. The working mechanism is opportunity registration: recording a named prospect with the carrier or master agent so the pursuit is protected for a defined period; unregistered pursuit is unprotected pursuit, and a deal worked for weeks can be lost to a direct rep or another agent with a registration. The unit also covers the etiquette and procedure when a prospect is already claimed - checking registration status early, respecting an active claim, and using the program's dispute path rather than racing to signature.

included: account crediting versus retail ownership
the opportunity-registration mechanism and its protection window
conduct when a prospect is already registered to another party
excluded: post-sale escalation and advocacy for existing customers, which is lifecycle territory
litigation over channel disputes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rules of engagement, registration procedure, or a concrete ownership dispute outcome changes the picture

pros.claim: Registering early converts pursuit effort into a defensible claim
pros.example: a registered franchise prospect stays credited to the agent even after a carrier direct team quotes the same sites

cons.claim: Registration windows expire and blanket-registering prospects to hoard them burns program goodwill
cons.example: a master agent flagging an operator who registered a hundred names it never contacted

failure_modes: working a deal for weeks before checking whether it is already claimed
assuming agency-model crediting means the agent can promise the customer account control it does not have
acceptance_tests: every active pursuit has a registration check on record before material effort is invested, and each registered opportunity notes its protection window
revisit_triggers: the program changes its rules of engagement or registration procedure
a deal is lost or disputed on ownership grounds

nodes.definition: Decide which small-business segments to pursue by asking where the internet-plus-backup bundle pays for itself out of the customer's own operations. Transaction-dependent retail and food service - card terminals, online orders, delivery tablets - lose measurable revenue every down minute, making backup a rational buy; multi-site operators (franchisees, clinics, small chains) multiply one relationship into many addresses and standardized deployments; field trades and mobile crews are mobility-first with a small office anchor; professional offices care about cloud application access and predictable support. Each targeted segment gets a profile: what it runs on, what an outage actually interrupts, which bundle layers plausibly apply, and who decides - so prospecting, discovery, and bundle design start from the segment's reality rather than a generic pitch.

included: segment profiles tied to operational dependence on connectivity
which bundle layers plausibly apply per segment
decision-maker patterns per segment
excluded: per-prospect fact finding, which is discovery's job
consumer and residential segments

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: segment-level win/loss or discovery evidence, or a portfolio change that reshapes servable segments

pros.claim: Segment profiles make the bundle case operational rather than generic
pros.example: walking into a taqueria knowing the conversation is about card terminals and delivery tablets staying up through an outage, not about connection speed tiers

cons.claim: Profiles harden into stereotypes that miss the individual business
cons.example: assuming every professional office tolerates downtime and skipping the accounting firm whose deadline week is existential

failure_modes: pursuing segments the carried carriers cannot plausibly serve in the operator's geography
targeting by ease of access instead of operational dependence, yielding accounts with no attach depth
acceptance_tests: each targeted segment has a written profile covering operational dependence, plausible bundle layers, and typical decision maker
revisit_triggers: deal outcomes or discovery findings repeatedly contradict a segment profile
the carrier portfolio's footprint or product set shifts which segments are servable

nodes.definition: Build the per-prospect fact base that every proposal must trace back to, gathered by asking and listening rather than assuming: what connectivity and phone services the business has today, with which providers, under what contracts and - critically - what end dates; what a down hour actually costs in the customer's own numbers (missed card transactions, idle staff, lost delivery orders); which applications and devices depend on the connection (POS, cloud back office, cameras, phones); how many sites and mobile lines exist; who decides and who signs. Discovery is honest in both directions: the agent does not inflate needs to justify attaches, and does not suppress facts (like a punitive early-termination clause on the incumbent contract) that argue for waiting. The fact base is written down, because it is the evidence the bundle design, the economics screen, and the disclosure pack all cite.

included: current services, providers, contracts, and end dates
downtime cost in the customer's own numbers
sites, lines, dependent applications, and decision makers
excluded: address serviceability verification, which is site qualification's work
designing the bundle, which consumes these facts downstream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-proposal corrections, changed customer facts, or a recurring gap in the discovery script

pros.claim: A written fact base makes every later artifact defensible and reusable
pros.example: the downtime figure the restaurant owner herself gave in discovery reappears verbatim in the backup section of the proposal

cons.claim: Thorough discovery costs a meeting that transactional prospects may not grant
cons.example: a walk-in prospect who wants a price today and balks at a structured conversation about contracts and downtime

failure_modes: proposing from assumptions and having the customer correct basic facts after the proposal is out
missing the incumbent contract end date and proposing a switch that triggers early-termination charges
acceptance_tests: every proposal traces each proposed service to a recorded discovery fact, and incumbent contract end dates are captured before any switch is proposed
revisit_triggers: the customer's operations, sites, or incumbent contracts change before close
a pattern of post-proposal corrections shows a discovery question is missing from the script

nodes.definition: Design the multi-service bundle as a layered architecture over one account: primary business internet is the anchor that wins the relationship; wireless (5G/fixed-wireless) backup is the first attach wherever discovery shows real downtime cost; managed Wi-Fi rides the same install; business mobile lines move the owner's and crew's phones under the same program; cameras and related services deepen the account where the program authorizes them. Each layer is simultaneously a distinct compensation stream under the program's mechanisms and a switching-cost anchor that makes the whole account harder to displace - but every layer must be earned by a discovery fact, not stacked because more streams pay more. The architecture is a template the account plan instantiates per customer: which layers apply here, in what order, and which are deliberately left out.

included: the anchor-plus-attach layer structure
each layer as both compensation stream and switching-cost anchor
the rule that every layer traces to a discovery fact
excluded: technical design of primary-plus-failover per site, which is site qualification's work
growing attach depth in later account years, which lifecycle management owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: attach-rate evidence by layer and segment, or a change in which products the programs authorize

pros.claim: A layered bundle multiplies revenue per acquisition without new prospecting cost
pros.example: one hardware-store relationship yielding internet, backup, four mobile lines, and a camera subscription across eighteen months from a single close

cons.claim: Deep bundles concentrate the customer's frustration if any layer underperforms
cons.example: a botched camera install souring an account that was happy with its internet and lines, putting every stream at risk at once

failure_modes: stacking layers no discovery fact supports and triggering buyer's remorse inside the chargeback window
designing a bundle around products the carried programs do not authorize the agent to sell
acceptance_tests: each bundle layer in a design names its discovery-fact justification and its program authorization, and omitted layers are marked deliberate
revisit_triggers: attach outcomes show a layer consistently failing to land in a segment
the program authorizes new attach products or retires existing ones

nodes.definition: Position 5G/fixed-wireless backup as the natural second stream on accounts whose own facts justify it. The case is built arithmetic-first from discovery: the customer's stated cost of a down hour, their remembered outage history, and what stops working when the primary fails (card payments, online orders, cameras, phones) - never from manufactured dread or worst-case storytelling. Where the numbers are real, backup converts a vague fear into a priced decision the customer can accept or decline; where discovery shows tolerable downtime - an appointment-only studio that can run a day on a phone hotspot - the honest move is not to attach, recorded as a deliberate omission. The strategy also frames what backup is: an automatic failover path for the site's essential traffic, with its actual per-address feasibility and configuration left to site qualification.

included: downtime-cost arithmetic from the customer's own facts
the no-attach rule when downtime is tolerable
framing backup as automatic failover for essential traffic
excluded: coverage checks, failover configuration, and testing - site qualification territory
fear-based outage rhetoric of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: changes in the customer's downtime exposure or in the territory's outage record

pros.claim: Customer-sourced downtime arithmetic sells backup credibly and keeps it sold
pros.example: a cafe owner who computed her own lost card revenue per down hour renews the backup line without being resold

cons.claim: Honest arithmetic shrinks the addressable attach base versus fear pitches
cons.example: conceding that the appointment-only studio genuinely does not need failover and booking one stream instead of two

failure_modes: selling backup on dramatized outage scenarios the customer's history does not support
promising failover behavior before site qualification has verified wireless coverage at the address
acceptance_tests: every backup attach cites the customer's own downtime cost and outage facts, and every declined attach on a qualifying account is recorded as a deliberate omission with its reason
revisit_triggers: the customer's operations change their downtime exposure (new delivery channel, new POS)
outage events in the operator's territory change the factual base of the case

nodes.definition: Attach the business's mobile lines - owner, crew, tablets, connected equipment - to the anchor account under the same program. Mobility is usually the highest-count attach: a five-person trades crew is five lines plus tablets, each carrying a per-line ongoing compensation mechanism, and consolidated billing under one program deepens the relationship the anchor started. The attach conversation is timed off trust earned by the anchor install, not forced into the first close, and it is honest about the friction: number porting from the incumbent, device and contract timing on existing lines, and coverage reality where the crew actually works - with porting logistics and coverage verification executed downstream, not promised casually. The unit covers when mobility leads instead: for field-trade segments with no meaningful office footprint, lines can be the anchor and fixed internet the attach.

included: per-line ongoing mechanism as the attach's economic shape
timing the attach off anchor trust
mobility-led ordering for field-heavy segments
excluded: executing ports and activations, which is activation coordination downstream
any specific per-line rate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: customer headcount/fleet changes or program mobility product changes

pros.claim: Line count scales the ongoing stream with the customer's headcount at near-zero acquisition cost
pros.example: a plumbing company that grows from four to seven techs adds three compensated lines with a phone call

cons.claim: Mobility carries consumer-grade expectations and support noise into a business relationship
cons.example: the owner calling the agent about a cracked phone screen as if the agent were the device vendor

failure_modes: pushing line migration before incumbent device contracts allow a clean exit
promising coverage where the crew works without flagging it for verification
acceptance_tests: each mobility attach records existing line count, incumbent contract timing, and a coverage-verification flag for the crew's working area before proposal
revisit_triggers: the customer's headcount or fleet changes
the program changes its mobility product set or per-line mechanism

nodes.definition: Deepen qualifying accounts with adjacent services the program authorizes: managed Wi-Fi (guest and back-office networks that ride the primary install), connected cameras and monitoring-adjacent services, fixed voice lines where the program carries them, and connected-device subscriptions. Each adjacent attach is screened three ways before it enters a design: the current program authorizes the agent to sell it (authorization lists change and differ by program tier), a discovery fact supports it (a retail floor wanting guest Wi-Fi, a stockroom shrinkage problem for cameras), and the agent can stand behind the sale at handoff (someone competent installs and supports it, per the program's delivery model). Adjacent services are where over-bundling temptation is strongest because each adds a stream, so the deliberate-omission discipline applies with full force.

included: the three-way screen: program authorization, discovery support, deliverability
managed Wi-Fi, cameras, fixed voice, connected-device subscriptions as attach classes
deliberate-omission discipline against over-bundling
excluded: install execution and support handoff mechanics, which are downstream
products outside the program's authorization, which are referred not sold

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: authorization list changes or support-burden evidence on an attach class

pros.claim: Authorized adjacent services turn one install visit into several sticky streams
pros.example: the camera subscription added at the hardware store makes the whole account materially harder for a competitor's internet-only offer to displace

cons.claim: Each adjacent service class carries its own failure surface into the account
cons.example: a flaky guest Wi-Fi portal generating weekly complaints on an account whose internet never blinked

failure_modes: proposing a product the current program tier does not authorize and retracting it after signature
attaching services no one competent is positioned to install or support
acceptance_tests: every adjacent attach in a design passes the three-way screen with the authorization source and date recorded
revisit_triggers: the program's authorized product list or tier changes
support burden evidence shows an attach class costing more than its stream justifies

nodes.definition: Instantiate the bundle architecture for one customer as a written account plan: which layers apply here (each tied to its discovery fact), in what sequence, and on what timing - anchored to real dates like the incumbent contract's end, the seasonal calendar of the business, and the trust milestones of a new relationship (clean install first, mobility conversation after the first quiet month). The plan maps each layer to its compensation mechanism class so the operator can see the account's expected stream shape - what pays once at activation, what pays ongoing - without ever attaching invented figures. It also right-sizes: for the smallest customers the plan may be two layers and deliberately stop, because the plan is a promise of relevance, not a quota. The finished plan is the artifact the economics screen evaluates and the lifecycle KB inherits.

included: layer selection with discovery-fact ties and sequencing dates
mapping layers to mechanism classes for stream shape
right-sizing for the smallest customers
excluded: executing later-phase attaches and growing the account in-life, which lifecycle owns
revenue projections with specific figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in underlying discovery facts or an executed phase deviating from plan

pros.claim: Date-anchored sequencing prevents both premature pushes and forgotten opportunities
pros.example: the plan holding the mobility conversation until the incumbent's device contracts lapse in March, then surfacing it automatically

cons.claim: Plans decay as customer facts change and stale plans mislead
cons.example: a plan still sequencing a second-site attach after the customer shelved the expansion

failure_modes: planning attaches the discovery facts never supported
sequencing a switch before the incumbent contract end date captured in discovery
acceptance_tests: every planned layer carries its discovery-fact tie, mechanism class, and sequencing date or milestone, and small-account plans show the right-sizing decision
revisit_triggers: a discovery fact underlying the plan changes
an executed phase lands differently than planned (declined, delayed, expanded)

nodes.definition: Screen each planned deal for whether it is worth pursuing under the carried program's actual mechanisms, reasoning in mechanism terms rather than invented numbers: how much of the deal's value arrives as activation cash exposed to the chargeback window versus ongoing streams that require the account to survive and the agent to stay compliant; how stable this customer looks against that chargeback window (tenure of the business, contract intent, payment reputation); how much unpaid effort the deal demands (multi-visit discovery, custom design) against the stream shape it plausibly yields; and whether the timing collides with the incumbent's early-termination exposure. The screen produces a go, a shaped go (fewer layers now, more later), or a documented no - and its verdicts feed back into which segments and deal shapes the operator keeps pursuing.

included: activation-versus-ongoing weighting under chargeback exposure
customer stability and unpaid-effort assessment
go / shaped-go / documented-no verdicts
excluded: tracking realized compensation against expectation, which is lifecycle work
any calculation using invented specific figures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: chargeback/cancellation outcomes or a change in mechanism mix and windows

pros.claim: Mechanism-level screening kills net-loss deals before effort is sunk
pros.example: declining a heavy custom design for a pop-up business unlikely to outlive the chargeback window

cons.claim: Screens calibrated too conservatively starve the funnel of learning deals
cons.example: rejecting every young business and never developing the new-business segment that later matures into stable accounts

failure_modes: chasing activation cash on customers likely to cancel inside the chargeback window
screening against remembered comp terms instead of the current guide
acceptance_tests: every screened deal records its verdict with the mechanism-level reasoning and the program-terms check date it relied on
revisit_triggers: chargeback or cancellation outcomes contradict the screen's stability judgments
the program's mechanism mix or chargeback windows change

nodes.definition: Assemble the proposal so that every material fact a signing customer needs is stated in it before signature, as a standing template rather than a per-deal improvisation: the contract term and what ending it early costs as an exposure class; promo pricing with its expiry date and what the price becomes after roll-off; exactly who bills (the carrier, on its paper) and who the customer calls for support; the agent's authorized-agent status; which services are contingent on serviceability confirmation at the address and therefore not yet promises; and the incumbent-contract timing facts discovery captured, so the customer can see the switch is timed to avoid early-termination charges. The pack exists because disputes about undisclosed terms destroy accounts, chargebacks, and program standing simultaneously - and because a proposal that discloses first is the concrete artifact of the ethics guardrails.

included: the mandatory disclosure set: term, early-exit exposure class, promo roll-off, billing and support identity, agent status, serviceability contingency
the standing template that enforces the set on every proposal
incumbent-timing transparency
excluded: contract drafting and legal review of carrier paper
quoting figures not verified against the current program that day

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dispute tracing to a disclosure gap, or program changes to terms that must be disclosed

pros.claim: A standing disclosure template makes the honest proposal the cheap default
pros.example: the promo roll-off line is printed by the template on every quote, so no deal depends on the agent remembering to mention it

cons.claim: Full disclosure hands hesitant buyers reasons to stall
cons.example: a prospect fixating on the after-promo price line and asking to think it over

failure_modes: a proposal silent on promo roll-off that detonates at the first post-promo bill
presenting a serviceability-contingent service as a settled promise
acceptance_tests: every issued proposal contains all six disclosure elements, and contingent services are visually marked pending address confirmation
revisit_triggers: a dispute or complaint traces to something the pack did not disclose
program terms change what must be disclosed (new promo structures, new contract forms)

nodes.definition: Manage the tension of carrying more than one carrier program. A second program is added for documented gaps - target-area addresses the lead carrier cannot serve, product classes it lacks (no fixed-wireless backup product, weak mobility), or concentration risk after a program-stability scare - never because a recruiter dangled a richer headline mechanism. The costs are real: split volume slows progress toward every program's better tiers (tier thresholds are mechanisms read from each guide), doubles the verification and portal burden, and creates the daily temptation to steer customers toward whichever program pays the operator better. The balancing rule is fit-first: when two carried carriers can both serve a customer, the recommendation follows coverage, product fit, and the customer's stated needs, with the operator's compensation difference explicitly excluded from the recommendation logic - a discipline that must be visible in the recorded reasons.

included: documented-gap justification for adding a program
volume-dilution and burden costs as mechanisms
the fit-first recommendation rule between carried carriers
excluded: initial portfolio construction, which precedes this unit
per-address serviceability determinations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: gap closure by the lead program, or evidence of comp-steered recommendations

pros.claim: A gap-justified second carrier rescues deals the lead program would strand
pros.example: a target strip mall unserved by the lead carrier's wired footprint closing on the second carrier's fixed-wireless product

cons.claim: Every added program dilutes tier progress and doubles operational surface
cons.example: missing the lead program's support-tier threshold in the exact quarter volume was split toward a new second carrier

failure_modes: adding programs for headline mechanisms until no carrier sees meaningful volume
steering customers to the better-paying program against fit and calling it judgment
acceptance_tests: each program addition cites its documented gap, and dual-serviceable recommendations record fit-based reasons with compensation difference excluded
revisit_triggers: the lead program closes the gap that justified the second carrier
a recommendation pattern suggests compensation is leaking into carrier choice

nodes.definition: Enforce the boundary that serviceability is address-specific fact-finding performed by the site qualification process, never assumed at the strategy table. Coverage maps, a neighbor's working service, and a carrier's marketing footprint are leads, not facts: fiber can stop one parcel short, and a strong outdoor 5G signal can die in a metal-roofed stockroom. Every proposal therefore marks which services are contingent on address confirmation, and the handoff to site qualification is a defined package: the exact service addresses, the candidate services per address (primary type, backup, lines), the discovery constraints that shape the survey (POS location, camera positions, hours a visit can happen), and the deadline the proposal's timing implies. Strategy resumes only when qualification returns per-address answers - and a failed address returns the deal to bundle redesign, not to improvised promises.

included: the never-assume rule for address serviceability
the handoff package: addresses, candidate services, survey constraints, timing
the return path when an address fails qualification
excluded: performing the checks, surveys, ordering, and failover testing - that is the site qualification KB's whole scope

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: qualification outcomes contradicting assumed coverage, or a changed intake contract downstream

pros.claim: A defined handoff package lets qualification run without re-interviewing the customer
pros.example: the surveyor arrives knowing the POS counter location, the stockroom camera spots, and that visits must happen before opening hours

cons.claim: The contingency discipline delays commitment and can cost impatient deals
cons.example: a prospect who wanted a signed promise today walking when told the backup line depends on an address check

failure_modes: promising service from a coverage map and unwinding the deal when the address fails
handing qualification bare addresses without the discovery constraints, forcing repeat customer contact
acceptance_tests: every proposal's contingent services are marked as such, and every handoff package contains addresses, candidate services, survey constraints, and timing
revisit_triggers: qualification results contradict the assumed footprint in a target area
the site qualification process changes what its intake package needs

nodes.definition: Close this KB's scope by handing the finished account plan to lifecycle management in a form it can operate on: the expected stream map per layer stated as mechanism classes (which layers pay at activation, which pay ongoing, under which program), every date the plan turns on (contract term start and end, promo expiry, planned attach milestones, incumbent contract dates still relevant), the discovery fact base and its last-verified date, and the deliberate omissions with their reasons so a future upsell conversation starts informed rather than re-selling a declined layer. Bundle strategy explicitly does not track whether compensation arrives as the mechanisms promise, does not run renewals or win-back, and does not handle carrier escalations - it delivers a plan whose promises are all verifiable, then stops. A handoff is complete when lifecycle can answer what was sold, why, on what dates, and what was deliberately not sold, without calling the seller.

included: the handoff contents: mechanism-class stream map, all plan dates, fact base, deliberate omissions
the completeness test for a finished handoff
excluded: compensation tracking, renewals, churn management, and escalation handling - the lifecycle KB's whole scope

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lifecycle intake feedback or a change in its expected handoff contents

pros.claim: A complete handoff makes the account operable by whoever manages it next
pros.example: eighteen months later the renewal conversation opens from the recorded promo expiry and the declined-camera reason instead of a cold file

cons.claim: Handoff rigor is overhead that feels pointless while the seller and manager are the same person
cons.example: a solo operator skipping the written stream map and losing the plan's dates when the account count hits fifty

failure_modes: handing off sold services without the dates the plan turns on
omitting the deliberate-omission record so lifecycle re-pitches a layer the customer already declined with reasons
acceptance_tests: each handoff passes the completeness test: sold layers with mechanism classes, all operative dates, the fact base with verification date, and deliberate omissions with reasons
revisit_triggers: lifecycle reports handoffs missing operative information
the lifecycle KB's intake expectations change

edges.why_related: which entry doors exist and what they demand depends on which channel model the operator is entering
which compensation mechanisms can exist at all follows from who bills and who owns the account
account crediting and rules of engagement are defined relative to the channel model in force
mechanism summaries are only valid when read from the current guide the verification discipline supplies
the distributor route is one of the entry doors the qualification decision opens for evaluation
which carriers are even accessible for the portfolio depends on the chosen entry route
compensation mechanism fit is one of the five portfolio selection criteria
servable segments follow from the carried carriers' footprint and product breadth
the segment profile shapes which discovery questions matter for a given prospect
every bundle layer must trace to a captured discovery fact
the backup attach is the architecture's first attach layer, instantiated by this strategy
the mobility layer's place and timing come from the architecture's layer structure
adjacent services are the architecture's deepening layers, screened before entering a design
the account plan instantiates the general architecture for one specific customer
the screen evaluates the concrete plan, not an abstract deal idea
the proposal presents the plan's selected layers with their terms disclosed
screen verdicts across deals supply the evidence for when a portfolio gap is real
the proposal's contingency markings define exactly what the qualification handoff must resolve
the lifecycle handoff packages the finished account plan and its dates
discovery must be honest in both directions - no inflated needs, no suppressed contrary facts
the no-fear-selling rule binds how outage risk may be framed in the backup case
the proposal must state the agent's authorized-agent status and who actually bills
adjacent services may only be sold where the current program authorization extends
no proposal issues without a same-cycle check of the terms it discloses
the screen must reason from the current mechanism mix, never a remembered one
an account plan is only built for prospects whose registration status permits the pursuit
the screen's stream-maximizing logic pressures toward attaches and timing the guardrails forbid
edges.resolution_rule: fit-first wins: a layer discovery does not support is removed no matter how it screens, and the screen may only shape or defer what ethics already allows

edges.why_related: adding carriers for coverage fights the selection logic of concentrating volume behind a lead program
edges.resolution_rule: a second program is added only for a documented gap (address, product class, or concentration risk) that strands target deals; absent a documented gap, concentration behind the lead program wins

edges.why_related: the distributor split reduces every mechanism's yield, arguing against the access it buys
edges.resolution_rule: route by realistic volume: below the requirement class for direct entry the split is the price of access and the master route wins; once sustained volume approaches direct-entry class, re-evaluate toward direct

edges.why_related: the drive to attach backup pressures against discovery findings of tolerable downtime
edges.resolution_rule: discovery facts win: no backup attach without customer-evidenced downtime cost, and the declined attach is recorded as a deliberate omission rather than retried each visit

edges.why_related: an attractive segment can be effectively closed because its accounts are registered to carrier direct or other partners
edges.resolution_rule: rules of engagement dominate: pursuit shifts to prospects and segments where the agent's registration can hold, and claimed accounts are contested only through the program's dispute path

edges.why_related: the segment's operational profile causes which bundle layers plausibly apply and in what order
the program's mechanism mix causes the stream shape the plan sequences toward
bundle depth and layer choice drive the deal's stream shape and thus its screen verdict
discovery completes before a proposal is assembled so every proposed service has a fact behind it
the lifecycle handoff finalizes only after qualification resolves which contingent services are real
accumulated no-verdicts and chargeback outcomes in a segment feed back into which segments stay targeted
repeated address failures in target areas feed back into whether the carried footprint matches the geography
both are attach layers that ride the anchor relationship and add per-service ongoing streams under program authorization

conflict_axes.name: fit_first_vs_comp_maximization
conflict_axes.description: The recommendation that fits the customer's discovered needs and the one that yields the operator the best stream mix are often different carriers or bundle depths.
poles: shape recommendations toward the better-paying option
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fit-first is absolute for carrier choice and layer inclusion; compensation may only influence sequencing among options fit already approved

conflict_axes.name: bundle_depth_vs_right_sizing
conflict_axes.description: Each added layer is another stream and more switching cost, but small operators can be oversold into remorse, cancellation, and chargebacks.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: every layer needs a discovery-fact tie; for the smallest buyers start narrow and let the account plan sequence later layers on earned trust

conflict_axes.name: direct_program_vs_master_agent_route
conflict_axes.description: Direct agreements keep the whole mechanism yield and build carrier standing but demand volume and back-office capacity; the distributor route grants access and support for a permanent split.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide by realistic volume and capacity, re-deciding when sustained volume approaches direct-entry class

conflict_axes.name: carrier_concentration_vs_coverage_breadth
conflict_axes.description: Concentrating volume builds tier standing with one program but strands unserviceable target addresses; carrying more carriers covers more addresses but dilutes every relationship.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: concentrate by default; add a program only on a documented address, product, or concentration-risk gap

conflict_axes.name: real_urgency_vs_fear_selling
conflict_axes.description: Downtime exposure is often genuinely urgent for transaction-dependent businesses, yet urgency framing slides easily into manufactured dread.
poles: convey the real cost of downtime
avoid fear as a sales lever
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: urgency may only be expressed through the customer's own numbers and history; if their facts do not carry the case, the case is not made

conflict_axes.name: quoting_speed_vs_term_verification
conflict_axes.description: Prospects reward same-day quotes, but every unverified quote risks resting on a changed program guide.
poles: verify current terms before any commitment
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: verification is non-negotiable for commitments; speed comes from making the portal check a fast standing routine, not from skipping it

conflict_axes.name: carrier_alignment_vs_customer_advocacy
conflict_axes.description: The agent is paid by and bound to the carrier's program yet wins accounts by being the customer's trusted connectivity advisor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: represent affiliation truthfully, then advise within it honestly: disclose what the program binds, recommend by fit, and refer needs the program cannot serve

conflict_axes.name: deal_speed_vs_serviceability_certainty
conflict_axes.description: Signing while the prospect is hot conflicts with the fact that no address is known serviceable until qualification proves it.
poles: hold commitments until the address is verified
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sign the relationship, not the unverified promise: proposals mark contingent services and the close is structured around confirmation

conflict_axes.name: activation_cash_vs_ongoing_patience
conflict_axes.description: Activation-heavy selling pays now and funds the young business, while account-based streams pay slowly but compound into the book that is the business's real value.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: screen deals by chargeback-adjusted stream shape: activation cash from unstable customers is often a net loss, while stable accounts justify patience

conflict_axes.name: full_disclosure_vs_closing_friction
conflict_axes.description: Every disclosed term - promo roll-off, contract length, contingencies - is honest and also a fresh reason for a hesitant buyer to stall.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure is not negotiable; friction is managed by disclosing early and matter-of-factly through the standing template rather than at the last minute

edge_cases.description: A prospect says 'so you're the carrier, right?' mid-pitch, revealing they think they are dealing with the network operator directly
edge_cases.trigger: customer confusion about who the agent is
edge_cases.mitigation: correct the misunderstanding on the spot in plain words - authorized agent, carrier bills and supports - and ensure the proposal restates it in writing

edge_cases.description: The carrier publishes a comp plan and promo revision between proposal issue and signature
edge_cases.trigger: a program guide change lands while a deal is in flight
edge_cases.mitigation: re-verify against the new bulletin before signature and re-issue the proposal if any disclosed term moved, logging both check dates

edge_cases.description: A strip-mall address the coverage map shows as served turns out to have no fiber path to the suite
edge_cases.mitigation: because the proposal marked the service contingent, return the deal to bundle redesign (different product or second carrier) instead of unwinding a promise

edge_cases.description: A worked prospect turns out to be registered to another agent through the same master
edge_cases.trigger: a registration check or dispute reveals a prior claim
edge_cases.mitigation: stop pursuit, use the program's dispute path only if the claim looks lapsed, and tighten the habit of checking registration before investing effort

edge_cases.description: A customer asks directly what the agent earns on the recommended bundle
edge_cases.trigger: a compensation transparency question in the sale
edge_cases.mitigation: answer honestly at mechanism level - paid by the carrier at activation and as the account stays - within program confidentiality, and never invent or misstate figures

edge_cases.description: A single-owner shop with limited English is ready to sign a five-layer bundle after one visit
edge_cases.trigger: a vulnerable buyer accepting scope they may not understand
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the close, explain in plain language, right-size the starting bundle, and leave the written proposal for review before signature

edge_cases.description: Discovery reveals the incumbent contract runs eight more months with a punitive early-exit clause
edge_cases.trigger: incumbent contract timing blocks an immediate switch
edge_cases.mitigation: disclose the exposure, plan the switch at contract end with a dated follow-up, and win interim trust with services that do not trigger the clause

edge_cases.description: An appointment-only studio with negligible downtime cost is on the attach list for backup
edge_cases.trigger: the attach playbook meets a customer whose facts do not support it
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the no-attach rule, record the deliberate omission with its reason, and keep the account on the plan for layers its facts do support

edge_cases.description: A customer's first post-promo bill jumps and they claim they were never told
edge_cases.trigger: promo roll-off lands without a remembered or written disclosure
edge_cases.mitigation: the standing template's roll-off line and the signed proposal are the defense; if the disclosure is genuinely absent, remediate with the carrier and fix the template gap

edge_cases.description: The master agent is acquired and re-papers sub-agent agreements with different terms
edge_cases.trigger: a structural change at the distributor mid-book
edge_cases.mitigation: read the new agreement before continuing to sell, compare against direct entry given current volume, and re-run the portfolio decision if terms degraded

edge_cases.description: Both carried carriers can serve a customer and the poorer product fit pays the operator a better mix
edge_cases.mitigation: recommend by fit with the reason recorded and the compensation difference explicitly excluded from the logic

edge_cases.description: A customer asks for an enterprise product the program does not authorize the agent to sell
edge_cases.trigger: demand outside the current authorization list
edge_cases.mitigation: say so plainly, refer through the carrier's proper channel or a qualified partner, and keep the authorized layers of the relationship

workflow.action: Map the channel models and place each candidate program on the map
workflow.description: Write down who bills, who supports, and who owns the account for every program considered
workflow.artifact: channel model map with per-program placement
workflow.gate: each program is classified agent, reseller, or referral with its three-way split recorded

workflow.action: Stand up the program-terms verification discipline
workflow.description: Define the current-truth artifacts, the pre-commitment recheck rule, and the check log
workflow.gate: the rule that no commitment issues without a same-cycle terms check is in force and logged

workflow.action: Fix the affiliation and ethical-selling guardrails
workflow.description: Adopt the disclosure-first, no-fear-selling, vulnerable-buyer, and truthful-affiliation rules that bind all selling
workflow.artifact: selling rules sheet covering representation and conduct
workflow.gate: customer-facing materials pass the representation rules and the conduct rules are written and adopted

workflow.action: Qualify into programs by the chosen route
workflow.description: Choose direct or distributor entry per program from current application terms and execute the agreements
workflow.artifact: executed program or sub-agent agreements with obligations summarized
workflow.gate: each entered program's route, requirements, and obligations are recorded from current terms before signature

workflow.description: Score candidate programs on footprint, breadth, mechanism fit, stability, and conflict exposure; name the lead
workflow.gate: every carried program is scored on all five criteria with the lead program and complement roles named

workflow.action: Define target segments from the carried portfolio
workflow.description: Profile the segments whose operations justify the bundle and whom the portfolio can plausibly serve
workflow.gate: each segment profile ties operational dependence to plausible bundle layers and a decision-maker pattern

workflow.description: Capture services, contracts and end dates, downtime cost in the customer's numbers, sites, lines, and deciders
workflow.gate: the fact base covers contracts with end dates, downtime cost, dependencies, and decision makers before design starts

workflow.action: Design the bundle and the account revenue plan
workflow.description: Instantiate the layer architecture for this customer with discovery ties, mechanism classes, and sequencing dates
workflow.artifact: account plan with layer justifications and dates
workflow.gate: every planned layer has a discovery-fact tie and a mechanism class, and omissions are marked deliberate

workflow.action: Screen the deal's economics at mechanism level
workflow.description: Weigh chargeback-exposed activation against ongoing streams, customer stability, and unpaid effort
workflow.artifact: screen verdict record (go / shaped go / documented no)
workflow.gate: the verdict cites mechanism-level reasoning and the date of the program-terms check it relied on

workflow.description: Issue the proposal from the standing template with all six disclosure elements and contingency markings
workflow.gate: all six disclosures are present and contingent services are visibly marked pending address confirmation

workflow.action: Hand off to site qualification with the full package
workflow.description: Deliver addresses, candidate services, survey constraints, and timing to the qualification process
workflow.gate: the package contains addresses, per-address candidate services, discovery constraints, and the deadline

workflow.action: Hand the finished account plan to lifecycle management
workflow.description: Package the mechanism-class stream map, operative dates, fact base, and deliberate omissions
workflow.gate: lifecycle can state what was sold, why, on what dates, and what was deliberately omitted without asking the seller

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because the channel model map, the current-terms discipline, truthful affiliation, and the selling guardrails define what every later choice is allowed to be; program qualification, the distributor route, portfolio selection, and engagement rules then establish which programs the operator can honestly sell; segment targeting and discovery ground the market view in verified facts; the bundle architecture and its attach strategies convert facts into layered stream designs; the account plan, economics screen, disclosure pack, and multi-carrier balance turn designs into defensible commitments; and the two handoff nodes close the KB's scope by passing verified packages to site qualification and lifecycle management.

dominance_rules.rationale: program terms, compensation plans, and product availability change without notice, and a commitment on stale terms fails at order time or in a dispute
dominance_rules.trigger: any quote, proposal, signature, or promise to a customer or carrier
dominance_rules.action: block the commitment until the current guide, comp bulletin, and availability are checked and the check is logged

dominance_rules.rule: Discovered fit dominates compensation in every recommendation
dominance_rules.rationale: steered recommendations churn, chargeback, and destroy the trust the ongoing-compensation model depends on
dominance_rules.trigger: a recommendation where the better-paying option and the better-fitting option differ
dominance_rules.action: recommend the fit choice and record the fit reasons with the compensation difference excluded from the logic

dominance_rules.rationale: implying carrier status is a program-termination offense that can forfeit the entire ongoing book
dominance_rules.trigger: any customer-facing material or conversation where the relationship could be misread
dominance_rules.action: state the authorized-agent relationship plainly and correct customer misunderstanding the moment it surfaces

dominance_rules.rationale: serviceability is address-specific; coverage maps and neighboring installs prove nothing about this parcel and suite
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to promise service before qualification has confirmed the address
dominance_rules.action: mark the service contingent in the proposal and structure the close around confirmation instead of promising

dominance_rules.rationale: an undisclosed term surfaces later as a dispute that costs the account, the compensation, and program standing at once
dominance_rules.trigger: temptation to soften or omit a term - promo roll-off, contract length, early-exit exposure - to smooth a close
dominance_rules.action: issue only proposals containing the full disclosure set, delivered early and matter-of-factly

dominance_rules.rule: Rules of engagement dominate pursuit of a claimed account
dominance_rules.rationale: racing a registered claim to signature burns program goodwill and usually loses the crediting anyway
dominance_rules.trigger: discovery that a prospect is registered to carrier direct or another partner
dominance_rules.action: stand down and pursue only through the program's dispute path if the claim appears lapsed

dominance_rules.rationale: an oversold small buyer cancels inside the chargeback window and the harm compounds beyond the one account
dominance_rules.trigger: a small or unsophisticated buyer accepting scope beyond what discovery supports
dominance_rules.action: right-size the starting bundle, explain in plain language, and leave the proposal for unhurried review

dominance_rules.rationale: invented commission, price, or savings figures are misrepresentations that surface in bills and disputes
dominance_rules.trigger: any impulse to quote a figure not verified against the current program that day
dominance_rules.action: speak in mechanisms and verified terms only, and fetch the current figure from the program before quoting it

dominance_rules.rule: Incumbent contract timing dominates activation urgency
dominance_rules.rationale: a switch that triggers the customer's early-termination charges converts a win into a grievance
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed switch while the incumbent contract's exposure window is still open
dominance_rules.action: disclose the exposure and sequence the switch at contract end unless the customer knowingly accepts the cost in writing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the current program guide before any quote or proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-issued proposals, walked-back commitments, and disputes built on retired terms

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run discovery before designing the bundle or writing the plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning the bundle after the customer corrects assumed facts the first design rested on

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check registration status before investing material pursuit effort
anti_rework_rules.prevents: weeks of worked deal lost to a prior claim that a first-day check would have surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm program authorization for every attach product before it enters a design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retracting proposed services after signature because the tier never authorized them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark every unconfirmed service serviceability-contingent in the proposal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding promised deals when the address fails qualification

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture incumbent contract end dates during discovery, not at close
anti_rework_rules.prevents: proposals that die on early-termination exposure discovered at signature

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the sub-agent agreement's exit and portability terms before signing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at a master's acquisition that the book and its streams are not portable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the disclosure set into the standing proposal template once
anti_rework_rules.prevents: per-deal disclosure improvisation and the disputes each forgotten line seeds

iteration_protocol.trigger: a carrier or master publishes a program guide, comp plan, or availability change
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify terms, refresh every in-flight proposal against the new bulletin, and update mechanism summaries and screens

iteration_protocol.trigger: repeated serviceability failures accumulate in a target area
iteration_protocol.action: re-examine the carrier portfolio's footprint fit and retune segment targets to what the carried carriers can serve

iteration_protocol.trigger: a deal is lost or disputed on account-ownership grounds
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the registration-first habit and adjust pursuit rules for the affected segment

iteration_protocol.trigger: discovery findings repeatedly contradict a segment profile or a bundle layer's assumed fit
iteration_protocol.action: revise the segment profile and the architecture's layer applicability for that segment

iteration_protocol.trigger: the master agent changes splits, is acquired, or drops a carrier
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the governing agreement, re-run the route decision against current volume, and revisit the portfolio

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, cancellation, or chargeback traces to selling conduct or a disclosure gap
iteration_protocol.action: repair the affected account honestly, then fix the guardrail or template gap that allowed it

iteration_protocol.trigger: an attach layer's outcomes materially lag the plan across accounts
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the layer's positioning and the economics screen's assumptions about its stream contribution

iteration_protocol.trigger: lifecycle management reports handoffs arriving incomplete or stale
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the handoff completeness checklist and re-verify fact bases older than their last-verified discipline allows
